subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Should OpenClaw add a core provider-family model fallback contract here, and if so should the canonical shape be wildcard/auto refs, explicit fallback-family groups, catalog-derived fallbacks, or no new core config surface?
rationale: The implementation cannot be chosen mechanically because each option creates a different public config/provider-routing contract with different upgrade, auth, quota, and user-expectation behavior.

options.title: Choose one core fallback contract
options.body: Define one public provider-family fallback shape, prefer canonical `openai/*` refs over legacy `openai-codex/*`, and require runtime, docs, tests, and migration/doctor alignment before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to catalog-derived fallback only
options.body: Treat the open catalog-derived fallback PR as a separate narrower feature and leave wildcard/auto or grouped-family behavior for a later design issue.

options.title: Keep flat fallbacks for now
options.body: Decline new core config surface until a stronger user/release signal justifies changing model-routing semantics beyond explicit flat fallback lists.

recommendation.title: Choose one core fallback contract
recommendation.body: Define one public provider-family fallback shape, prefer canonical `openai/*` refs over legacy `openai-codex/*`, and require runtime, docs, tests, and migration/doctor alignment before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The model fallback path and product-scope history point most strongly to steipete for the canonical config/runtime contract decision.
